speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me how long it has been there and if it started as a small bump or blister?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis (suspected) due to travel or exposure history; however, given her immunosuppression from Crohn's and steroid use, we must also rule out atypical mycobacterial infection or cutaneous tuberculosis. REQUEST TEST: Wound Culture (bacterial and fungal) and PCR for Leishmania. REQUEST IMAGES: Clinical photos of the lesion to assess borders and granuloma formation.
